title: A dark disk or co-rotating substructure: would a slow, co-rotating dark-matter component change anything for the 248 keV event at delta ~ 300 keV?
question: Does a slow co-rotating dark-matter component (dark disk: v_lag 0-100 km/s, sigma 30-90 km/s, fraction f_DD of a fixed rho_0 = 0.3) change the inelastic rates, modulation phase, 16 June LR, elastic companion count, exothermic rate or Higgsino window inferred from the LZ event?
headline_result: No: <= 6e-10 of any such component lies above 700 km/s, so every inelastic rate at delta = 250-380 keV is exactly (1-f_DD) x SHM with unchanged phase and LR(16 June); Higgsino delta(N=1) shifts -0.6/-2.2 keV (f = 0.1/0.3); elastic N_lo rises x1.17/1.65; the exothermic ROI rate falls (x0.87 at f = 0.2) because the integrated down-scatter rate is velocity-independent and the disk's peak at E* = 267-339 keV lies beyond the 270 keV roll-off
model_or_mechanism: composite (1-f) Baxter-SHM + f isotropic Gaussian dark disk co-rotating at V0 - v_lag, fixed rho_0; analytic Earth-frame eta and exact non-central chi-square tail fractions; per-stream WimPyDD kernels (own O1/O6; P058 iso endo/exo and P068 Higgsino/L10 caches), 1 TeV, 93 days
confidence: high - analytic kinematics and kernels validated against P003/P006/P007/P034/P055/P058/P068 anchors to 1-4 %; disk parameters recalled but conclusions hold across the whole range
agent_tools: Read x21, Bash x12, Write x5, Edit x17
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1 (erf, stats.ncx2); pandas 3.0.5; matplotlib 3.11.2; WimPyDD 2.0.4 (diff_rate per-stream kernels, v_earth_sun, streamed_halo_function validation); common/lzcommon.py
